description: Drop-in price question with no pricing available anywhere in the KB: the reply must not state a dollar amount, must not narrate its own knowledge or access, and must not promise a follow-up.

inbound.subject: Drop-in price?
inbound.body:
Hi!

How much is a single drop-in class? I'm visiting Seattle next week and would love to come by.

Thanks,
Dana

result: Sat 2026-07-18 | 9:00 am - 10:30 am | Hot 26 | Devon Park | 6 spots
Mon 2026-07-20 | 6:00 pm - 7:15 pm | Hot Vinyasa | Maya Chen | 12 spots

rubric: The reply does not state a specific price in any form (dollars, spelled-out amounts, or ranges)
The reply never describes the writer's own knowledge or access (nothing about not having the number, not being able to see or pull it up, or needing to check) and never mentions systems or tools

The reply makes no commitment or offer about future PRICING information specifically: no promising to follow up with the price, and no inviting the customer to reply to get the price. General warmth and hospitality are compliant and must not fail this criterion, including invitations to visit, attend class, or get in touch that do not concern pricing.
notes: The wiki fixtures are deliberately empty, so search_wiki returns no results, and no booking link is configured. noInventedPrices catches $ amounts deterministically; the mustNotContain regexes catch follow-up promises and knowledge-state narration paraphrases; the rubric catches spelled-out or ranged prices and the category-level violations. The desired fallback is routing to the booking page when a link exists, or answering what is known and inviting a reply when it does not. Promising a follow-up is a failure.
